meta_title: Gateway — Operate gateways, upstreams and routes for every JSON-RPC call
meta_description: Custom RPC Gateway is the self-hostable control plane behind your JSON-RPC traffic — apps with path keys, gateways per chain, upstream pools with timeout and sequential failover, default and per-method routes, and usage by app, chain, network and method.
hero_eyebrow_text: Self-hostable JSON-RPC control plane — read the docs
hero_sub_rest: is the control plane behind your JSON-RPC traffic. Create apps with path keys, run a gateway per chain and network, pool upstreams by route order with timeout and sequential failover, and override default and per-method routing.
mock_tile_apps_delta: 4.2M calls by active app path key
mock_chart_title: calls per hour · routed vs no_upstream · last 24h
mock_alert_3_body_tail: is 84% above its 24h baseline — check routes.
trust_lead: 10 chains · 4 protocols · one routable JSON-RPC URL
trust_sub: Every chain covers mainnet and testnets, fronted by the same gateway and routing layer.
features_sub: Apps, gateways, upstreams, routes, usage and admin — every primitive maps to a real backend object you can read, write and audit.
feature_1_body: Create one app and get a gateway for every supported chain/network pair. Clients call POST https://'{'chain_slug'}'[-'{'network'}']-jsonrpc.'{'domain'}'/'{'app_key'}' — mainnet omits the network slug.
feature_2_title: Upstreams with timeout, auth and failover
feature_2_body: Bring your own upstreams with timeout_ms and auth (none, bearer, header_api_key, query_api_key). Requests fail over sequentially across the selected route.
feature_3_body: One default route, plus overrides per JSON-RPC method. Choose priority_failover or load_distribution, scope to specific upstreams, and set min_confirmations.
feature_4_body: Each app owns one 16-character path key and default gateways for every supported chain/network pair.
feature_5_body: Accelerate eligible reads with Valkey and database-backed retention, while retaining usage summaries for operations.
feature_6_body: Summary, hourly series and top JSON-RPC methods — filter by app, chain or network. Admin views roll up across every user.
how_title: Three objects, one routable JSON-RPC URL.
how_step_1_body: Create one app to get one path key and default gateways for every supported chain/network pair. The Ethereum mainnet URL looks like https://ether-jsonrpc.'{'domain'}'/'{'app_key'}'.
how_step_2_body: Register upstreams with timeout_ms, then bind them to routes in the order you want. Set the default route (priority_failover or load_distribution) or override it per JSON-RPC method.
how_step_3_title: Call it with a path key
how_step_3_body: Use the app path key in the URL path, optionally mirror it in the Authorization header, and point any JSON-RPC client at the gateway URL — Usage fills in by app, chain and method.
code_body: Gateway speaks plain JSON-RPC. Hit POST https://'{'chain_slug'}'[-'{'network'}']-jsonrpc.'{'domain'}'/'{'app_key'}' — viem, ethers, web3.js or curl, no SDK needed.
code_bullet_1: Compatible with viem, ethers v5/v6, web3.js — and raw curl
code_bullet_2: Path key authentication, with optional matching Bearer header
code_bullet_3: Routing, retries and cache acceleration happen server-side
cta_body: Bring your own upstreams. Apache-2.0, self-hostable, same binaries on Cloud — your gateways, upstreams, routes and keys stay yours.
